distractors.A: read the hands the wrong way round

distractors.E: swapped the hands and read 6 as 6 minutes

questions.stem: A bottle holds 1.5 litres of water. Sam pours out 3 glasses of 250 mL each. How much water is left in the bottle?
A bakery made 156 muffins. It sold 89 in the morning and 38 in the afternoon. How many muffins were left?
questions.explanation: Sold altogether: 89 + 38 = 127. Left: 156 − 127 = 29.

distractors.A: only took away the morning sales

questions.stem: A train leaves at 15:25. What is this in am/pm time?
questions.explanation: After midday, subtract 12 from the hour: 15 − 12 = 3. So 3:25 pm.

distractors.C: it is after midday, so pm
distractors.E: 24-hour times are not written with pm

questions.stem: Which fraction is equal to 3/4?
questions.explanation: Multiply the top and bottom by 3: 3/4 = 9/12.

questions.stem: A rug is 3 m long and 2 m wide. How many square tiles, each 1 m by 1 m, would it take to cover the same area?
questions.explanation: Area = 3 × 2 = 6 square metres, so 6 tiles.

questions.stem: Mrs Lo has 75 stickers. She gives 8 stickers to each child until she can't give any more full sets of 8. How many stickers are left over?
questions.explanation: 8 × 9 = 72, so 9 children get 8 stickers. 75 − 72 = 3 left over.

distractors.A: that is the number of children

questions.stem: Ruby saves $4 every week. How many weeks will it take her to save $50?

questions.stem: There are 30 students in a class. 2/5 of them walk to school and 1/3 ride bikes. The rest come by car. How many come by car?
questions.explanation: 2/5 of 30 = 12 walk. 1/3 of 30 = 10 ride. 30 − 12 − 10 = 8 come by car.

distractors.E: that is walkers plus bike riders

questions.stem: Tess has between 10 and 30 marbles. When she puts them into groups of 4, there are 3 left over. When she puts them into groups of 5, there are 2 left over. How many marbles does she have?
questions.explanation: Numbers between 10 and 30 that leave 3 when grouped in 4s: 11, 15, 19, 23, 27. Which leave 2 when grouped in 5s? Only 27 (5 × 5 + 2).

questions.explanation: Buses leave at 7:10, 7:35, 8:00, 8:25… Mia arrives at 8:15, so the next bus is at 8:25: a wait of 10 minutes.

questions.stem: Ella's party is 45 days after 20 May. May has 31 days and June has 30 days. What is the date of the party?
questions.explanation: From 20 May to 31 May is 11 days. 45 − 11 = 34 days left. June uses 30 more days (to 30 June), leaving 4: 4 July.

distractors.D: forgot June has 30 days to get through

questions.stem: A tank holds 120 L of water. It leaks 4 L every hour, and a tap adds 10 L every 2 hours. How much water is in the tank after 6 hours?
questions.explanation: In 6 hours the leak loses 6 × 4 = 24 L, and the tap adds 3 × 10 = 30 L. 120 − 24 + 30 = 126 L.

questions.stem: Ava has only 10c and 20c coins. She has 12 coins worth $1.80 altogether. How many 20c coins does she have?
questions.explanation: If all 12 were 10c coins, they would be worth $1.20. The extra 60c comes from 20c coins, each worth 10c more: 6 coins. So 6 × 20c + 6 × 10c = $1.80 ✓.

distractors.C: 9 × 20c is already $1.80, with no coins left over

questions.stem: A square is cut into 4 identical rectangles placed side by side. Each rectangle has a perimeter of 20 cm. How long is each side of the square?
questions.explanation: Each rectangle is as long as the square's side and a quarter as wide. Perimeter = 2 × (side + quarter side) = 2½ sides = 20 cm, so the side is 8 cm (rectangles 8 cm × 2 cm).

distractors.D: that is the width of a rectangle

questions.stem: Pens come in packs of 6 for $4 or packs of 10 for $6. What is the cheapest way to buy exactly 30 pens?
questions.explanation: Options for exactly 30 pens: 3 packs of 10 = $18; 5 packs of 6 = $20; (a mix would need 30 = 6a + 10b, e.g. 0 × 6 + 3 × 10 is the only other way). The cheapest is $18.

questions.stem: Lena gave half of her stickers to her brother, then gave 6 stickers to a friend. She had 9 stickers left. How many stickers did she start with?
questions.explanation: Work backwards: before the friend she had 9 + 6 = 15. That was half of what she started with, so she started with 30.

distractors.C: halved and added in the wrong order
